bio_en: Abraham Gyulkhandanian was born on 13 August 1875 in Vagharshapat, studied at the Gevorgian seminary and joined the ARF in 1894. From 1898 he worked in Baku, organising most of the Armenian workers under the ARF and winning them gains such as the eight-hour day; in the Armenian-Tatar clashes he was the ARF Bureau's representative in Ganja, organising self-defence and the punishment of officials who had incited the violence. Arrested in 1910 in the Lyzhin trial, he spent two years in prison, then returned to Baku, chaired the Baku National Council from 1917 and with Rostom led the defence of Baku in 1918. He died in Montmorency near Paris on 1 January 1946, three months after his release from a long imprisonment in 1944-45.
